label: late original-phase steps (t>=7) of long sequences, preferring certain input tokens (i,v,m,l,3,h,b,2)
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase and only at late positions: never before t=5, about 1% of mass at t=5-6 combined being small (t=6 ~9%), and ~90% of mass at t=7-8, i.e. the last one or two input tokens of L=8-9 sequences (L=9 holds 71% of mass). Never fires at the delimiter or in the copy phase. Position alone (phase 0, t>=7) has mass recall 0.90 but precision only 0.22; within that window the input token matters (i, v, m, l, 3, h, b, 2 have the highest rates), and adding that token set raises dev F1 to 0.53 (precision 0.52, mass recall 0.66). Rate also rises with the number of digits in the sequence and with first token y/r/g, but adding first_tok did not improve F1. Magnitude is largest at t=7-8 on the listed tokens; remaining structure looks like a distributed hidden-state code not captured by a simple predicate.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: v, i, m, l, h, 3; least: n, f, r, a) and the first original token (most: y, r, g, t, 2, s; least: o, m, f, 1); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=8, t=7, t=6.
